rules: named-port data is never unwrapped by member name
canonical transport wrappers are resolved only at their declared binding boundary
only registered assertion outputs determine results
first violated assertion is terminal and cannot be masked by result selection
literal types, closed options and selector grammar validate before execution
exact approximate tolerances are explicit, nonnegative and alias-consistent
parsers preserve the selected complete data and fail closed
CSV Unicode scalar separators, final empty records and post-quote state are explicit
structured literal and immutable canonical object wildcard order follows unsigned Unicode scalar key ordering; parsed JSON and CSV header order remain parser-owned
native execution receipts bind the actually executed step prefix, selected assertion port, normalized DAG and all used operation, parser, selector and regex registry identities
release-bearing native receipts retain the loaded build identity, exact worker digest, worker protocol and device-time provenance; missing, altered or stale identities never establish current proof
a failed execution retains its exact loaded target identity and explicit inconclusive failure without fabricating completed steps or release-bearing observations
completed native evidence agrees with the executed observation prefix, selected assertion values and determination; canonical result fields cannot contradict retained execution evidence

invalid specifications stop before traversing more than the registered step limit; closed-shape and binding violations return bounded precise diagnostics with surrogate-safe 256-UTF-16-unit value previews, leaving submitted source unchanged

approximate operands and tolerances use only safe integer numbers without negative zero, canonical plain decimal strings, or closed typed DECIMAL objects with a string value; both aliases for a tolerance component must normalize to exactly the same mathematical value
tolerance arguments are admitted only for APPROXIMATE COMPARE EQ/NE or ASSERT_EQ; ordered COMPARE rejects APPROXIMATE and every tolerance argument at definition admission
retained prior-registry compatibility excludes COMPARE and ASSERT_EQ carrying APPROXIMATE or any tolerance input so affected numeric definitions require explicit migration and reverification

DECIMAL_STRING equality and all ordered decimal-string comparisons accept only string operands and remove only surrounding ASCII U+0009 through U+000D and U+0020 whitespace; no nonstring coercion or Unicode trim expansion
ordered COMPARE with explicit DECIMAL_STRING restricts both operands to the exact plain-decimal string domain; omitted mode and INTEGER retain safe-integer or plain-decimal-string ordering

SORT DECIMAL validates every item as the closed canonical typed DECIMAL representation including singleton collections; exact stable ASC order, reversed DESC order and original values are preserved; malformed typed domains use SORT_DOMAIN with UNDETERMINED

retained prior-registry compatibility also excludes DECIMAL_STRING equality, ordered comparisons and DECIMAL or inferred-domain SORT; unaffected ordinary exact comparisons and explicit nondecimal SORT retain their prior identity

SELECT_XML rejects every wholly empty segment including a final attribute selection as XML_PATH_MISSING with UNDETERMINED; existing empty text or attribute strings and nonempty partial matches retain exact document order

PARSE_JSON validates every decoded string value and member name with the shared Unicode scalar authority before admitting the parsed value; lone surrogates are MALFORMED_JSON with UNDETERMINED and valid pairs remain accepted

REGEX and ASSERT_MATCH distinguish finite outer quantifiers from unbounded outer quantifiers; actual nested unbounded repetition remains rejected under unchanged pattern, input, quantifier-count and worker limits

retained prior-registry compatibility excludes PARSE_JSON, SELECT_XML, REGEX and ASSERT_MATCH so affected earlier definitions require explicit migration and reverification; no old receipt is relabeled as current
